chapter: Armstrong band memories, Chicago players and Baltimore
title: Naming the Armstrong band
summary: Budd and Hinton list the personnel of Armstrong's 1933 band, including Scoville Brown, Oldham brothers, Wilson, Yank Porter and McKendrick.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But, anyway, getting back to ZT. ZT would write this hard music, then. But, this one, this is one time he did stick us. We really just couldn't play. We had -- oh, yeah. We had Scoville Brown in the band, too.
Saxophone player. Saxophone and clarinet. And, he --
Let's stop a second and see if we can name that band now, since we got it together there.
Okay. On saxophones we had Scoville Brown, George Oldham and myself.
On trumpets we had Stumpy Whitlock. His first name was Ellis. Ellis Whitlock. We had ZT.-- Zillion the T Randolph.
And, my brother, Cag Johnson on trombone. And, in the rhythm section we had Teddy Wilson, and later Charlie Beal. We had Yank Larson on drums, and later Harry Dewe. And, on bass --
Yeah. That was his name. What did I say, Porter, before?
I thought you said -- the one they sent from Chi -- to New York, again?
His name was Yank Larson, too?
Yank Porter. I'm very sorry. Nobody -- Yank Larson, the greatest --
Yeah. Yank Porter, and then later Harry Dowe.
And, on bass we had George Oldham.
And, on tenor guitar we had Mike McKendriks.
And, of course, there was Louie.
